prompt: Walter Winans won Olympic gold for shooting in 1908. What did he win gold for at the 1912 Games?
options: A bronze statuette of a horse
A painting of a stadium
A poem about sport
A march for orchestra
correctAnswer: A bronze statuette of a horse
explanation: His statuette An American Trotter won the first Olympic gold for sculpture. He is the only American to win medals in both the art and sport sides of the Games.

prompt: The Olympic art competitions were dropped because too few artists wanted to enter.
explanation: They were dropped after 1948 because most of the artists were professionals, and the IOC of the time insisted on amateurs. The 151 art medals no longer count in the official record.

prompt: The chimpanzee whose paintings were shown in Gothenburg in 1964 was passed off as a French artist named Pierre __________.
explanation: Pierre Brassau was really Peter, a four-year-old chimpanzee from the zoo at Borås. A journalist set up the show to test whether critics could tell modern art from monkey art.

prompt: According to Desmond Morris, what did Congo do if pressed to keep painting after he had decided a picture was finished?
options: He stubbornly refused
He painted over the whole picture
He tore the paper up
He started a second fan pattern on top
explanation: Stopped too early, Congo had a screaming fit; urged on after finishing, he refused. Morris took this as a hint of a very primitive sense of composition in an ape.

prompt: Match each name to its story:

pairs.right: Olympic gold for shooting and for sculpture
Won the 1912 literature gold under two pen names
Chimp whose paintings fooled most Gothenburg critics
Chimp whose paintings sold in 2005 when a Renoir and a Warhol did not

explanation: All four stories turn on the same question: how much the judging of art depends on who people think made it.

prompt: Why did the foundation that owns Borja's sanctuary start charging visitors one euro in 2012?
options: To pay the extra staff needed to manage the crowds
To pay for a professional restoration
To pay Cecilia Giménez a fee
To keep the number of visitors down
correctAnswer: To pay the extra staff needed to manage the crowds
explanation: Ticket money now goes to the foundation, including help for elderly residents without means at its nursing home. Plans to restore the fresco professionally were dropped.

prompt: The 2019 professional restoration of the St George of Estella recovered all of the carving's original paint.
explanation: After three months in a Pamplona laboratory, at a cost of €30,000 paid by the parish, the saint looked like himself again, but some original colors were lost forever.

prompt: In 1961 the Museum of Modern Art hung Matisse's paper cutout Le __________ upside down for 47 days.
explanation: Le Bateau means The Boat. A stockbroker noticed that the more complex shape, the reflection, was on top, which Matisse would not have done.

prompt: Why will the Düsseldorf museum keep Mondrian's New York City I hanging the way it has since 1945?
options: Its adhesive tapes are so loose that turning it could make them slip
Mondrian's will forbade moving it
The curators do not think it is upside down
Its frame cannot be taken off the wall
correctAnswer: Its adhesive tapes are so loose that turning it could make them slip
explanation: The curator says the tapes are hanging by a thread. She adds that the wrong orientation is now part of the work's story.

prompt: Match each artwork to what happened to it:

pairs.right: Repainted by an 81-year-old parishioner, then drew crowds of tourists
Carving given a pink face, then sent to a laboratory in Pamplona
Hung upside down at MoMA for 47 days
Probably upside down since 1945, left that way to protect it

explanation: Two of these are damage by well-meant hands; two are mistakes about which way is up. Each shows how much an artwork depends on the people who look after it.

prompt: What did visitors find when they crowded into Yves Klein's 1958 exhibition The Void in Paris?
options: An empty gallery with freshly whitened walls
A room full of blue paintings
A floor covered in gold leaf
A sculpture made of jets of air
correctAnswer: An empty gallery with freshly whitened walls
explanation: Klein emptied Galerie Iris Clert and painted it white, so the empty room was the exhibit. About 3,000 people lined up to see it, watched over by two uniformed Republican Guards.

prompt: Rauschenberg erased a de Kooning drawing without asking de Kooning first.
explanation: He asked de Kooning for a drawing to erase, and de Kooning, with some reluctance, agreed. Years later de Kooning called it "sort of a corny idea."

prompt: Buyers of Yves Klein's zones of immaterial pictorial sensibility paid for them in __________.
explanation: Three buyers chose to burn their receipts in a ritual while Klein threw half the gold into the Seine. Others kept the receipt, which made the zone resellable.

prompt: What did the buyer of Salvatore Garau's invisible sculpture Io sono receive in 2021?
options: A certificate of authenticity and instructions for displaying it
A sealed glass box said to contain air
An empty plinth signed by the artist
A video of the sculpture being made
correctAnswer: A certificate of authenticity and instructions for displaying it
explanation: The instructions call for a clear space about five feet by five feet. As with Klein's surviving receipt, the paperwork is what makes the work something that can be owned and sold again.

prompt: Match each work to what it consists of:

pairs.right: A rubbed-out sheet in a gilded frame
An invisible sculpture sold with a certificate
An empty plinth Andy Warhol once stepped on

explanation: All four ask what makes something an artwork when there is little or nothing to see. Usually the answer is the artist's name, the story and the paperwork.

prompt: How did Piero Manzoni set the price of each tin of Merda d'artista in 1961?
options: By its weight, at that day's price of gold
At a fixed price of 1,000 lire
By auction among his friends
He gave them away free
correctAnswer: By its weight, at that day's price of gold
explanation: At 1961 gold prices a tin cost about $37. Thirty years later Sotheby's sold one for $67,000, when the gold rule would have asked about $396.

prompt: Dr Félix Rey's drawing, found among Irving Stone's papers, shows that Van Gogh cut off only his earlobe.
explanation: The drawing shows that he removed the whole ear, leaving only a sliver of the lobe. The "only the lobe" story rested on Paul Signac, who never saw the ear uncovered.

prompt: Richard Serra's Tilted Arc, a curved steel wall 120 feet long, stood in Federal Plaza in __________ until it was removed in 1989.
explanation: It stood beside a federal office complex in lower Manhattan. The government commissioned it for $175,000 and later cut it into three pieces overnight.

prompt: Why did historians long believe that Van Gogh had cut off only his earlobe?
options: The painter Paul Signac, who visited him in hospital, wrote that he had
Van Gogh's self-portraits show the ear intact
Gauguin's memoirs said so
The hospital kept the ear and measured it
correctAnswer: The painter Paul Signac, who visited him in hospital, wrote that he had
explanation: Signac never saw the wound: Vincent wore a band around his head and a fur cap. Bernadette Murphy found Dr Rey's drawing in the Bancroft Library at Berkeley.

prompt: Match each person to their part in these stories:

pairs.right: Had a Manzoni tin opened in Marseille in 1989
Claimed in 2007 that the tins held plaster
Doctor who drew Van Gogh's wound
GSA official who held the 1985 Tilted Arc hearing

explanation: Each story turned on evidence that was hidden, disputed or ignored: a sealed tin, a folded doctor's note, and a hearing whose majority lost.
